safety_observation.name: safety_observation
safety_observation.description: A safety observation refers to any recorded note or report about workplace safety conditions, behaviors, or practices, whether positive or negative. In HSE, these observations are used to identify trends, reinforce safe behaviors, and highlight areas needing improvement before incidents occur.
examples: Observed all workers wearing proper PPE in the welding area.
Noted that emergency exits were kept clear during the shift.
Reported that forklift operators followed designated routes.
Saw a worker using a ladder correctly to access high shelves.
Identified good housekeeping practices in the chemical storage room.

near_miss.name: near_miss
near_miss.description: A near miss is an unplanned event that did not result in injury, illness, or damage but had the potential to do so. In HSE, near misses are critical for proactive risk management, as they highlight underlying hazards or unsafe conditions before they lead to actual incidents.
examples: A wrench fell from scaffolding but missed workers below.
Forklift nearly collided with a pallet due to obstructed view.
Worker slipped on a wet floor but regained balance without falling.
Overhead crane hook passed close to a worker’s head, no contact made.
Chemical container was almost knocked over but caught in time.

incident.name: incident
incident.description: An incident is any unplanned event that results in or could have resulted in injury, illness, property damage, or environmental harm. In HSE, incidents are formally reported and investigated to determine root causes and prevent recurrence.
examples: Worker sustained a laceration while using a box cutter.
Oil spill occurred during equipment maintenance.
Employee tripped over an extension cord and sprained ankle.
Fire alarm triggered due to electrical short circuit.
Forklift struck a storage rack causing minor damage.

hazard_report.name: hazard_report
hazard_report.description: A hazard report documents the identification of a potential source of harm or danger in the workplace. In HSE, these reports are used to address unsafe conditions or practices before they lead to incidents or injuries.
examples: Reported frayed electrical cords in the break room.
Identified missing guardrails on elevated platform.
Noted chemical storage area lacking proper signage.
Observed oil spill near loading dock.
Flagged blocked fire extinguisher access.

environmental_observation.name: environmental_observation
environmental_observation.description: An environmental observation records any condition, event, or behavior that may impact the environment, such as pollution, waste, or resource use. In HSE, these observations help monitor compliance with environmental standards and identify opportunities for improvement.
examples: Observed improper disposal of oily rags in general waste bin.
Noted excessive dust emissions from the crusher area.
Reported leaking coolant from machinery onto soil.
Saw recycling bins overflowing in the lunchroom.
Identified chemical drums stored without secondary containment.

quality_issue.name: quality_issue
quality_issue.description: A quality issue refers to any observation or report of a product, process, or service not meeting required standards or specifications. In HSE, quality issues can have safety or environmental implications if not addressed promptly.
examples: Found welds not meeting inspection criteria on pressure vessel.
Reported paint peeling from newly coated surfaces.
Identified incorrect labeling on chemical containers.
Noted missing bolts on assembled equipment.
Observed packaging damage on incoming materials.

maintenance_request.name: maintenance_request
maintenance_request.description: A maintenance request is a formal or informal notification that equipment, machinery, or infrastructure requires repair, servicing, or inspection. In HSE, timely maintenance requests help prevent equipment failures that could lead to safety or environmental incidents.
examples: Requested repair for leaking hydraulic hose on excavator.
Submitted work order for malfunctioning emergency lighting.
Reported broken guard on conveyor belt.
Notified maintenance of faulty smoke detector in warehouse.
Asked for inspection of noisy ventilation fan.

unsafe_condition.name: unsafe_condition
unsafe_condition.description: An unsafe condition is any physical state or environmental factor in the workplace that could cause harm or injury if not corrected. In HSE, reporting unsafe conditions is essential for hazard control and accident prevention.
examples: Found water pooling near electrical panels.
Observed missing handrails on stairway.
Noted poor lighting in storage area.
Identified loose tiles on walkway.
Reported exposed wiring in maintenance room.

unsafe_act.name: unsafe_act
unsafe_act.description: An unsafe act is any behavior or action by a person that increases the risk of an accident or injury. In HSE, identifying and correcting unsafe acts is crucial for fostering a safe work culture and preventing incidents.
examples: Worker bypassed machine guard to speed up process.
Employee climbed shelving to retrieve item instead of using ladder.
Operator used mobile phone while driving forklift.
Technician failed to lock out equipment before maintenance.
Worker did not wear required eye protection in grinding area.

first_aid_case.name: first_aid_case
first_aid_case.description: A first aid case is an event where an injury or illness occurs at work and is treated with on-site first aid, without requiring professional medical attention. In HSE, tracking first aid cases helps monitor minor injuries and identify areas for safety improvement.
examples: Worker received a bandage for a small finger cut.
Employee treated for minor burn with cold water and ointment.
First aid administered for insect sting on arm.
Worker had eye washed after dust exposure.
Employee given ice pack for minor ankle sprain.

month.name: month
month.description: In HSE analytics, 'month' refers to a calendar period of approximately 30 days used for tracking, reporting, and analyzing safety observations, incidents, and trends. Monthly aggregation helps identify recurring issues, seasonal patterns, and the effectiveness of interventions within a specific timeframe.
examples: Five near misses were reported in the month of March.
Monthly safety inspection completed for April.
No lost time injuries occurred this month.
Monthly environmental audit identified two minor spills.
PPE compliance improved compared to last month.

quarter.name: quarter
quarter.description: In the HSE context, 'quarter' denotes a three-month period used for summarizing and comparing safety performance, incident rates, and compliance trends. Quarterly analysis supports management reviews, regulatory reporting, and strategic planning for health, safety, and environmental improvements.
examples: Quarterly incident rate decreased compared to previous quarter.
Q2 safety training completion reached 98%.
Quarterly review identified an increase in near misses.
No environmental violations reported this quarter.
Quarterly audit found three areas needing improvement.

year.name: year
year.description: In HSE analytics, 'year' refers to a twelve-month period used for comprehensive evaluation of safety performance, incident trends, and compliance with regulations. Annual data supports long-term planning, benchmarking, and reporting to stakeholders and authorities.
examples: Annual safety performance report shows a reduction in recordable injuries.
No major incidents occurred this year.
Yearly environmental targets were met.
Lost time injury frequency rate improved over the year.
Year-to-date, all workers completed mandatory safety training.

production.name: production
production.description: In HSE, the production department refers to areas and teams directly involved in manufacturing, assembly, or processing of goods. Observations here often relate to machine operation, line safety, process hazards, and worker behaviors during active production. Typical events include equipment malfunctions, unsafe work practices, or exposure to hazardous materials.
examples: Operator bypassed machine guard during shift on the assembly line.
Spill of coolant observed near production equipment.
Worker not wearing hearing protection in the manufacturing area.
Conveyor belt emergency stop was blocked by materials.
Unlabeled chemical container found in the production zone.

maintenance.name: maintenance
maintenance.description: The maintenance department handles repair, servicing, and upkeep of equipment and facilities. HSE observations here often involve lockout/tagout compliance, working at heights, electrical safety, and risks during equipment servicing. Incidents may include near misses with moving machinery or improper use of tools.
examples: Technician failed to apply lockout before starting pump repairs.
Oil spill left unattended in the maintenance workshop.
Improper ladder use observed during light fixture replacement.
Missing PPE during scheduled equipment servicing.
Loose tools found on top of operating machinery after maintenance.

quality_control.name: quality_control
quality_control.description: Quality control involves inspection, testing, and verification of products or processes to ensure standards are met. HSE issues in this department may include exposure to testing chemicals, improper sample handling, or ergonomic risks during repetitive inspection tasks. Observations often relate to safe laboratory practices and handling of rejected materials.
examples: Inspector not wearing gloves while handling chemical samples.
Broken glassware left on the quality lab bench.
Ergonomic strain reported during repetitive product inspections.
Spill of test reagent not cleaned up in the QC area.
Rejected parts stored in an unsafe manner in the inspection zone.

logistics.name: logistics
logistics.description: The logistics department manages the movement, storage, and distribution of materials and products. HSE observations here often involve vehicle safety, manual handling, loading dock hazards, and risks related to forklifts or pallet jacks. Incidents may include blocked emergency exits or unsafe stacking of goods.
examples: Forklift operated at excessive speed in the loading area.
Pallets stacked too high, creating a tipping hazard.
Blocked fire exit in the shipping zone.
Driver failed to chock wheels during unloading.
Manual lifting of heavy boxes without assistance observed.

administration.name: administration
administration.description: Administration covers office-based staff and activities such as HR, finance, and management. HSE concerns in this area include office ergonomics, fire safety, slips and trips, and emergency preparedness. Observations may also relate to visitor management and safe evacuation procedures.
examples: Blocked emergency exit in the administration office.
Loose electrical cords causing trip hazard near desks.
Improper storage of cleaning chemicals in admin area.
Fire drill not conducted for office staff this quarter.
Ergonomic assessment requested for administrative assistant.

safety.name: safety
safety.description: The safety department is responsible for developing, implementing, and monitoring health and safety policies and procedures. Observations here include safety audits, incident investigations, PPE compliance checks, and training sessions. This team often leads hazard identification and risk assessments across all departments.
examples: Safety officer conducted a walk-through and noted missing signage.
Incident investigation initiated by the safety department.
PPE compliance audit performed by HSE team.
Safety training session held for new employees.
Hazard report submitted to the safety office.

engineering.name: engineering
engineering.description: Engineering involves the design, modification, and technical oversight of equipment, processes, and facilities. HSE observations in this department may relate to design safety, risk assessments, technical reviews, and safe implementation of new systems. Issues can include inadequate guarding in new equipment or overlooked hazards in process changes.
examples: New machine design lacked adequate emergency stop features.
Engineering review identified potential pinch points in conveyor system.
Process change implemented without updated risk assessment.
Guarding not installed on prototype equipment.
Technical drawing omitted required safety signage.

warehouse.name: warehouse
warehouse.description: The warehouse department is responsible for storage and handling of raw materials, components, and finished goods. HSE issues here often involve manual handling, racking safety, forklift operations, and fire prevention. Observations may include blocked aisles, unsafe stacking, or improper use of lifting equipment.
examples: Aisle blocked by pallets in the warehouse.
Damaged racking observed during warehouse inspection.
Forklift parked in front of emergency exit.
Boxes stacked above safe height limit.
Manual lifting of heavy items without proper technique.

packaging.name: packaging
packaging.description: The packaging department handles the preparation and packing of products for shipment or storage. HSE concerns include repetitive motion injuries, machine guarding, use of sharp tools, and exposure to packaging materials. Observations may involve improper use of tape dispensers, unguarded machinery, or slips from spilled materials.
examples: Operator cut finger while using box cutter in packaging area.
Packaging machine missing safety guard.
Spilled packing material created slip hazard.
Repetitive strain reported by packer on the line.
Improper disposal of plastic wrap in packaging zone.

research_and_development.name: research_and_development
research_and_development.description: Research and development (R&D) involves experimental work, product development, and process innovation. HSE observations here often relate to chemical handling, laboratory safety, experimental equipment, and new process trials. Incidents may include spills, improper PPE use, or untested procedures.
examples: Chemical spill occurred during experimental trial in R&D lab.
Researcher not wearing eye protection while mixing reagents.
Unlabeled sample stored in laboratory fridge.
Fume hood alarm ignored during product development test.
Prototype equipment operated without safety review.
